as_told.title: Grusch: UFOs born secret under the Atomic Energy Act

tellings.quote: t. The term 'special nuclear material' means (1) plutonium, uranium enriched in the isotope 233 or in the isotope 235, and any other material which the Commission, pursuant to the provisions of section 51, determines to be special nuclear material, but does not include source material; or (2) any material artificially enriched by any of the foregoing, but does not include source material.

SEC. 51. SPECIAL NUCLEAR MATERIAL.—The Commission may determine from time to time that other material is special nuclear material in addition to that specified in the definition as special nuclear material. Before making any such determination, the Commission must find that such material is capable of releasing substantial quantities of atomic energy and must find that the determination that such material is special nuclear material is in the interest of the common defense and security, and the President must have expressly assented in writing to the determination.
c. The term 'atomic energy' means all forms of energy released in the course of nuclear fission or nuclear transformation.

r. The term 'Restricted Data' means all data concerning (1) design, manufacture, or utilization of atomic weapons; (2) the production of special nuclear material; or (3) the use of special nuclear material in the production of energy, but shall not include data declassified or removed from the Restricted Data category pursuant to section 142.

plain: A US law from 1954 may be the legal reason any material recovered from a crashed UFO is kept secret automatically. The idea comes from a witness named David Grusch, who tells Michels that the law's definition of "special nuclear material" (the category of nuclear stuff the government controls most tightly) "basically states any material that releases any kind of atomic energy," which would take in crash material. The law is the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, passed by Congress on 30 August 1954, and Michels repeats Grusch's reading on several episodes, once going further to say the wording was written "in a sneaky but deliberate way" to protect UFO secrets, and elsewhere saying anything recovered is "born secret," the common name for information that is classified from the moment it exists; an unidentified researcher on another episode repeats Grusch's words almost exactly. The Act itself defines special nuclear material as plutonium, enriched uranium, "and any other material which the Commission... determines to be special nuclear material," and it makes "Restricted Data" of "all data concerning" atomic weapons and the production or use of such material. But it allows that extra category only after the Commission finds the material "capable of releasing substantial quantities of atomic energy" and "the President must have expressly assented in writing," steps Grusch's paraphrase leaves out. So the law does set up the born-secret system the tellers describe, but it speaks of data and nuclear materials, and stretching its "other material" clause to a recovered craft is the tellers' reading, which the text neither states nor rules out. If they are right, a 1954 nuclear law would have quietly covered UFO wreckage for decades.

discussion.by: Atomic Energy Act of 1954 (Public Law 703, 83rd Congress, 68 Stat. 919)
discussion.text: The tellers' "born secret" is the common name for what the Act sets up: it defines Restricted Data as "all data concerning (1) design, manufacture, or utilization of atomic weapons; (2) the production of special nuclear material; or (3) the use of special nuclear material in the production of energy", restricted by its subject from the moment it exists, with the Commission charged "to control the dissemination and declassification of Restricted Data". Special nuclear material is plutonium and enriched uranium "and any other material which the Commission, pursuant to the provisions of section 51, determines to be special nuclear material", a determination the Commission may make only after finding the material "capable of releasing substantial quantities of atomic energy", and for which "the President must have expressly assented in writing to the determination"; Grusch's "any material that releases any kind of atomic energy" gives that clause without the finding and the assent. The gap is one of scope: the Act speaks of data and of nuclear materials, and reaching a recovered craft through the "other material" clause is the tellers' extension, which the text neither states nor excludes.

discussion.by: United States Code, 42 U.S.C. 2071 (Cornell Legal Information Institute)
discussion.text: The statute as it stands today lets the Commission add other material to special nuclear material only after finding it capable of releasing substantial quantities of atomic energy, says "the President must have expressly assented in writing to the determination", and has the determination and the assent sent to Congress's Energy Committees, with thirty days of session to pass, before it takes effect. The NRC is quoted in search results as saying it "has not declared any other material as special nuclear material", and no assent under the section is in the open record; the Justice Department's Office of Legal Counsel holds of presidential acts in general that they "remain effective upon a change in administration" until a later president acts, so an early written assent, had one been given, would stand until revoked. The open record holds no case of a president refused access to a special access program; it holds Clinton's remark in Belfast in 1995 that if the Air Force recovered alien bodies "they didn't tell me about it, either", Grusch's sworn statement of 2023 that he himself was "denied access" to the program's read-ons, and laws of 2022 and 2023 that require such programs to be reported to Congress's committees and congressional leadership, naming no role for the President, and no public document found classes recovered craft as special nuclear material.
